MUQATIL:100:1-6/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:100:1-6/r6.speaker: مقاتل
MUQATIL:100:1-6/r6.claim: Their galloping hooves raise dust as they break into the enemy’s gathering; the Muslims defeat and kill the opposing forces.

MUQATIL:100:1-6/r7.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:100:1-6/r7.speaker: مقاتل
MUQATIL:100:1-6/r7.claim: Gabriel tells Muhammad the victory has happened that day; Muhammad announces it to the believers, who rejoice, while God disgraces the Jews and hypocrites.

FARRA:v3p284#2/r6.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p284#2/r6.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p284#2/r6.claim: Naqʿ means dust or soil; its pronoun refers to an unmentioned valley, which context can supply because dust comes from a place.

FARRA:v3p284#2/r7.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p284#2/r7.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p284#2/r7.claim: A pronoun can refer to something known without a prior mention; the unexpressed referent in 97:1 is the Quran.

FARRA:v3p284#2/r8.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p284#2/r8.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p284#2/r8.claim: The sun is understood in 38:32 even though it has not been mentioned.

MAJAZ:v2p307/r4.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p307/r4.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p307/r4.claim: They raise dust, and naqʿ means dust.

TAB-FULL:v24p572/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p572/r6.speaker: ابن عباس وعلي
TAB-FULL:v24p572/r6.claim: In a conversation with Ali, Ibn Abbas first says the oath concerns horses raiding for God's cause and lighting cooking fires at night; Ali counters that Badr had only two horses and identifies the creatures as pilgrims' camels moving from Arafat through Muzdalifa to Mina, and Ibn Abbas recants.

TAB-FULL:v24p580/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p580/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p580/r1.claim: The phrase means the creatures raised dust in a valley; naqʿ means dust, also described as dirt. The pronoun in ‘bihi’ refers to an unmentioned place understood because dust must be raised from somewhere.

TAB-FULL:v24p580/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p580/r2.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p580/r2.claim: Mujahid identifies those who stir up dust as horses.

TAB-FULL:v24p580/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p580/r3.speaker: عطاء وابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p580/r3.claim: Ata and Ibn Zayd gloss naqʿ as dust.

TAB-FULL:v24p580/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p580/r4.speaker: عكرمة
TAB-FULL:v24p580/r4.claim: Ikrima says the horses raised dust and soil with their hooves.

TAB-FULL:v24p580/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p580/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p580/r5.claim: Qatadah says the horses stirred dust from the ground with their hooves.

TAB-FULL:v24p580/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p580/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p580/r6.claim: In Ali's interpretation of the oath as pilgrims' camels, the dust arises as animals tread the ground with hooves and feet between Arafat, Muzdalifa, and Mina.

TAB-FULL:v24p580/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p580/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
TAB-FULL:v24p580/r7.claim: Ibn Masud says they stir up dirt as they travel.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r1.claim: Asked about the oath, Ibn Abbas first says it means horses raiding for God and resting at night; Ali objects that Badr had only a few horses and says the camels run from Arafat to Muzdalifa and Mina, raising dust and reaching Jam. Ibn Abbas recants.

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3457#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says horses raid at dawn, kick up dust from their hoof marks, and reach the enemy group.

NAHHAS:v5p277/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p277/r16.speaker: الفراء
NAHHAS:v5p277/r16.claim: Al-Farra says 'by it' refers to the valley, understood from context though not previously mentioned.

NAHHAS:v5p277/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p277/r17.speaker: أبو الجوزاء عن ابن عباس
NAHHAS:v5p277/r17.claim: Abu al-Jawza reports Ibn Abbas's gloss of naqʿ as dust.

THALABI:v10p270/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p270/r12.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p270/r12.claim: Naqʿ means dust; wasatna bihi means entering the middle of a group, and the light, doubled, and derived forms all mean to enter the midst.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p323/r13.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p323/r13.speaker: قتادة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p323/r13.claim: One reported explanation attributed to Qatadah is that the animals raise dust; the segment begins citing Abd Allah ibn Rawahah as poetic evidence.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p327/r1.claim: The following Sūrat al-Qāriʿah is Meccan according to all the authorities mentioned.

QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r10.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r10.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p442/r10.claim: The horses raise dust as they go.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r1.claim: The root th-w-r describes dust or smoke rising, birds leaving their nests, and people surging toward an enemy; athara means to stir up.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r10.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r10.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r10.claim: The valley reading suits the view that the verses concern pilgrims' camels, since Wadi Muhassir is the known valley where they speed.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r11.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r11.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r11.claim: Abu Ishaq says bihi means the place where the animals ran; context indicates the place though it was not mentioned before.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r12.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r12.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r12.claim: Fa-atharna is coordinated with the sense of al-mughirat: those who raided at dawn then raised dust.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r2.speaker: امرؤ القيس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r2.claim: Imruʾ al-Qays uses atharna for raising dust along a rough path.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r4.speaker: جرير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r4.claim: Jarir's verse uses al-naqʿ for dust rising.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r5.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r5.claim: The commentators say the horses stir up dust with their hooves.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas recites Hassan's line describing horses raising dust between the two mountains of Kadaa.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r7.speaker: الكلبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r7.claim: Al-Kalbi takes bihi to mean the place where the horses ended their run.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r8.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r8.claim: Al-Farra takes bihi to refer to the valley; a pronoun may refer to a known thing even without prior mention.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v24p245#2/r9.claim: Qur'an 97:1 supplies an example of referring by pronoun to something not previously mentioned, with the Quran understood.

WAHIDI-QT:100:4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:100:4/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:100:4/r1.claim: Atharna means they stirred up dust in the place where they ran.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:100:1-8/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:100:1-8/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:100:1-8/r4.claim: The chargers stir dust where they run.

JISHUMI:v10p7511/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r1.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة وقتادة
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r1.claim: Al-Hasan, ʿIkrimah, and Qatadah say the surah is Meccan; another view says it is Medinan and was revealed around a raid.

JISHUMI:v10p7511/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r2.claim: A report promises ten good deeds for reciting the surah for every person who spent the night at Muzdalifah and witnessed Jamʿ.

JISHUMI:v10p7511/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r4.speaker: أبو حيوة
JISHUMI:v10p7511/r4.claim: Abu Haywah reads fa-atharna with a doubled thāʾ, a form carrying the sense of causing or intensifying the effect; the common reading is light.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p508/r14.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p508/r14.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p508/r14.claim: These descriptions are the objects of the oath.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p508/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p508/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p508/r9.claim: Atharna means the horses raised dust at the place where they ran; the location is left unstated because the sense makes it understood.

KASHSHAF:100:4/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:100:4/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:100:4/r1.claim: At that time the horses stir up dust.

KASHSHAF:100:4/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:100:4/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:100:4/r2.claim: Wasatna bihi may mean they reached the enemy's midst at that time or by means of the dust, or that they were enveloped in it.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r10.speaker: لبيد
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r10.claim: Labid’s poetic phrase about a true shout rising illustrates naqʿ as clamor.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r16.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r16.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r16.claim: Fa-atharna coordinates with the verb represented by the preceding active participle: the runners sparked, raided, and then raised dust.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r6.speaker: أبو حيوة
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r6.claim: Abu Haywah doubles the thāʾ in fa-atharna, meaning they brought out or displayed dust; the form may reflect reversal from thawarna and replacement of wāw by hamzah.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r8.claim: The pronoun in with it may refer to the dawn, dust, raiding place, or running implied by al-ʿādiyāt.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r9.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p793/r9.claim: Another figurative sense of naqʿ is shouting and commotion during a raid, supported by a prophetic expression and Labid’s verse.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p795/r8.claim: A report promises ten good deeds for reciting al-ʿĀdiyāt for every person who spent the night at Muzdalifah and witnessed Jamʿ.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r10.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r10.claim: The pronoun in bihi apparently means the morning, but can refer to a place supplied by context; horses are known to raise dust.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r11.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r11.claim: Ali says the camels raise the dust with their hooves.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r12.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r12.claim: A poem describes horses emerging from dense dust with bloody ears like pen tips.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p514/r9.claim: Naqʿ is rising, scattered dust; Abu Haywa reads fa-atharna with doubled tha.

TABRISI:100:1/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:1/r1.speaker: أبو حياة
TABRISI:100:1/r1.claim: Abū Ḥayāt has a rare reading with doubled thāʾ in atharna.

TABRISI:100:1/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:1/r3.speaker: ابن جني
TABRISI:100:1/r3.claim: Ibn Jinnī derives doubled atharna from displaying, like showing engraving; its hamza is radical, unlike the added hamza of the light form meaning to stir.

TABRISI:100:1/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:1/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:100:1/r8.claim: Naqʿ means dust in which a person is immersed as in water.

TABRISI:100:4-11/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:100:4-11/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:100:4-11/r1.claim: Atharna means they stirred up dust; the pronoun in bihi refers to an understood place or valley where the horses ran.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p206#2/r5.claim: In the expedition account, the horses snort through their nostrils, spark with their hooves on stones, attack at dawn, raise dust, and reach the enemy together.

RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r6.speaker: محمد بن كعب
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r6.claim: Muhammad ibn Kaʿb says the dust rises along the route between Muzdalifah and Mina.

RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r9.speaker: أبي عن النبي
RAZI-FULL:v32p60#2/r9.claim: A report attributed to Ubay and raised to the Prophet promises a reward measured by the number who spend a night at Muzdalifah and witness Jamʿ.

RAZI-FULL:v32p62#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p62#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p62#3/r1.claim: نقع can mean dust, explained either by its rising or by the image of sinking into water; it can also mean funeral wailing, as in a prophetic report.

RAZI-FULL:v32p62#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p62#3/r2.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
RAZI-FULL:v32p62#3/r2.claim: A prophetic saying uses نقع for mourning cries; in the context, the horses stir dust where they raid through their forceful charge.

RAZI-FULL:v32p62#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p62#3/r3.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v32p62#3/r3.claim: Al-Farraʾ says به refers indirectly to the place where the raid ends, since the preceding phrase establishes that a raid must occur somewhere.

RAZI-FULL:v32p62#3/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p62#3/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p62#3/r4.claim: Alternatively, به refers to the time when the attack took place.

RAZI-FULL:v32p62#3/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p62#3/r5.speaker: الكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v32p62#3/r5.claim: Al-Kisaʾi says به refers to the enemy, mentioned earlier in the oath.

RAZI-FULL:v32p62#3/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p62#3/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v32p62#3/r6.claim: The verb فأثرن coordinates with the verbs implied by the preceding active participles: the mounts ran, sparked, raided, and then raised dust.

RAZI-FULL:v32p62#3/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v32p62#3/r7.speaker: أبو حيوة
RAZI-FULL:v32p62#3/r7.claim: Abu Haywa reads the verb with a doubled ث, meaning they brought out or displayed dust; the reading may also reflect a change from ثرن to وثرن and then hamza.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:4#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:4#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:100:4#2/r1.claim: The softened form of the verb is illustrated by the Quranic phrase about people stirring the earth.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:4/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:4/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:100:4/r1.claim: The horses raise dust through their forceful running at the place they raid.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:4/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن رواحة
QURTUBI-FULL:100:4/r2.claim: Ibn Rawaha's poem describes horses stirring dust at the sides of Kida.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:4/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:100:4/r3.claim: The pronoun in bihi refers to the place where the raid occurs; Arabic may refer to an unstated place when context makes it clear.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:4/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:100:4/r4.claim: Another reading makes bihi mean by the running, which has already been mentioned in context, they stirred dust.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:4/r5.speaker: محمد بن كعب القرظي
QURTUBI-FULL:100:4/r5.claim: Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi identifies al-naq as the route or stretch between Muzdalifa and Mina; it may mean dust raised from that place.

QURTUBI-FULL:100:4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:100:4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:100:4/r6.claim: Lexicons define al-naq as dust, a pool or collected water in a well, and free land that gathers water; the term has several plurals.

BAYDAWI-FULL:100:1-5/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:100:1-5/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:100:1-5/r5.claim: Atharna means they stirred up dust or shouting, by that time.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p353#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p353#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p353#4/r1.claim: At that time, the horses stir up dust.

QASHANI:100:1-4/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:100:1-4/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:100:1-4/r6.claim: Discipline exhausts, refines, and thins the body and denies appetites as the soul turns intensely to God in love.

QASHANI:100:1-4/r7.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:100:1-4/r7.speaker: author
QASHANI:100:1-4/r7.claim: The powers leave bodily concerns to follow heart and spirit and receive lights; raising dust means wasting the body to dust.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r10.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r10.claim: Abū ʿUbayda also glosses naqʿ as raising one's voice, citing Labīd.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p526/r9.claim: Naqʿ means dust; two poetic citations use it for dust raised in battle.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p528/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p528/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p528/r10.claim: Fa-atharna coordinates with the active participle as a verb in meaning: the runners ran, raided, then raised dust.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p528/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p528/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p528/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī instead says the clause coordinates with the verb replaced by the active participle.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p528/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p528/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p528/r13.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says doubled atharna means they revealed dust or proposes a word reversal; Abū Ḥayyān calls the reversal contrived.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p529/r4.claim: Another interpretation understands naqʿ here as shouting.

SAMIN-DURR:100:3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:3/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:100:3/r3.claim: One view takes all the racing, sparking, and raiding descriptions as horses; their descriptions are coordinated in sequence as in a cited poetic example.

SAMIN-DURR:100:3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:3/r4.speaker: أمير المؤمنين
SAMIN-DURR:100:3/r4.claim: A view attributed to the Commander of the Faithful takes the descriptions as camels running from ‘Arafa to Muzdalifa and Mina; a poem by Safiyya bint ‘Abd al-Muttalib supports this interpretation.

SAMIN-DURR:100:4#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:4#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:100:4#2/r1.claim: On the cry interpretation of naq‘, the preposition ba means ‘in’, and the pronoun refers back to the place where the raid occurred.

SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r1.claim: ‘Fa-atharna’ coordinates a verb with a noun phrase because the noun is a relative participle standing for a verb; the underlying sequence is ‘those that ran, sparked, raided, then raised’.

SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r10.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r10.speaker: أبو عبيد
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r10.claim: Abu Ubayd says naq‘ can mean raising one’s voice and supports it with a line about a sincere cry.

SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r11.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r11.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r11.claim: Al-Zamakhshari also permits naq‘ to mean a cry, citing a Prophetic expression and a line by Labid; on this reading the horses stirred the people attacked at dawn.

SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhshari describes the verb as coordinated with the verb for which the active participle stands.

SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r3.claim: The pronoun in ‘bihi’ may refer to dawn, meaning that they raised dust at dawn; the author calls this good because dawn is explicitly named.

SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r4.claim: The pronoun may instead refer to the unmentioned place, since stirring dust requires a place and the scene and verb imply one; al-Zamakhshari calls it the place of the raid.

SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r5.claim: A third view makes the pronoun refer to the enemy, implied by the charging horses.

SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r6.claim: The common reading has a light thā’ from athara (‘scatter and raise’); Abu Haywa and Ibn Abi ‘Abla read it doubled.

SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r7.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r7.claim: Al-Zamakhshari explains the doubled reading either as making dust manifest, or through a far-fetched metathesis from thawrna and conversion of wāw to hamza; the author says the latter is very remote and not a regular sound change.

SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r8.claim: Changing an open wāw to hamza is not a regular rule; the few examples such as ahad and anah are exceptional, so they do not justify this derivation.

SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:100:4/r9.claim: Naq‘ means dust; poems by an unnamed poet and Ibn Rawaha use it for dust raised by horses.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p465#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p465#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p465#2/r3.claim: The horses raise dust at the place where they clash and fight.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p466#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p466#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p466#2/r2.claim: The dust is raised at the place the runners arrive, whether on pilgrimage or in a military expedition.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p466#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p466#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p466#2/r4.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says the Prophet sent horses on an expedition and heard no news for a month; the surah then revealed, and al-Bazzar calls the report very unusual.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p509/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p509/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p509/r1.claim: During a raid horses charge in changing directions as combatants pursue or meet the enemy; the force of their movement raises abundant dust.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p509/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p509/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p509/r2.claim: The phrase means that the horses raise dust through the raid's action, place, and time; their cries and neck movements make it gather and swirl around them.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p509/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p509/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p509/r4.claim: The oath's horses also suggest human thought: people can bring sound meanings and proofs, or corrupt ideas and falsehood, into either unbelieving or believing groups.

BIQAI-FULL:v8p509/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p509/r5.speaker: الحديث القدسي
BIQAI-FULL:v8p509/r5.claim: A sacred hadith is cited to show that even in battle, complete devotion belongs to the servant who remembers God while facing an opponent.

DURR-FULL:v8p600/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r10.claim: The horses raise dust with their hooves as they run.

DURR-FULL:v8p600/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r4.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v8p600/r4.claim: Their hooves raise dust from the ground.

DURR-FULL:v8p601/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r1.claim: The raised naqaʿ is dust from the ground stirred when hooves and camel feet tread on it.

DURR-FULL:v8p601/r13.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r13.claim: Ibn Abbas says the horses raise dust.

DURR-FULL:v8p601/r20.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r20.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p601/r20.claim: The dust is raised by the horses’ hoofbeats.

DURR-FULL:v8p602/r12.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r12.speaker: عطية
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r12.claim: Atiyya says the horses raise dust.

DURR-FULL:v8p602/r16.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r16.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas defines naqaʿ as dust rising from horses’ hooves; Hassan ibn Thabit’s verse supplies Arab usage evidence.

DURR-FULL:v8p602/r17.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r17.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r17.claim: Hassan ibn Thabit’s line is cited as evidence that horses stir dust at Kadaa.

DURR-FULL:v8p602/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r2.claim: Qatada reads the passage as horses running until panting, striking sparks with their hooves, raiding at dawn, raising dust, entering the people’s gathering; kanud means ungrateful.

DURR-FULL:v8p602/r23.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r23.speaker: ابن مسعود
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r23.claim: Ibn Masud says the camels raise dust as they go.

DURR-FULL:v8p602/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p602/r6.claim: Mujahid says horse impacts raise dust.

BURSEVI:v10p383/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p383/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p383/r8.claim: Atharna means they stirred up dust at that time; the form derives from athawara, with the wāw's vowel transferred and its replacement by alif followed by elision.

BURSEVI:v10p383/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p383/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p383/r9.claim: The pronoun in “thereby” may refer to the time or to the raid, with the preposition indicating cause or accompaniment; naq‘ means dust.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r1.claim: Atharna means stirred up; its underlying form contracted as the wāw's vowel moved back, became alif, then dropped before another still letter.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r10.speaker: عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r10.claim: ʿUmar allowed women to weep for Khālid while seated, provided there was no loud wailing or clamor.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r11.claim: Other possible pronoun antecedents are the enemy or the raid, with bā read as causal, associative, or locative; the morning reading is clearest and most elegant.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r2.claim: The verb may coordinate with the preceding noun phrase or active participle, which has verbal force; there is no grammatical anomaly and no need to posit an omitted verb.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r3.speaker: ابن المنير
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r3.claim: He says switching from participles to a verb vividly depicts the action in the imagination, more strongly than a sequence of nouns.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r4.speaker: ابن معد يكرب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r4.claim: His poem illustrates vivid sequential depiction by moving from an imperfect verb to a series of perfect verbs.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r5.speaker: الطيبي
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r5.claim: He says the three horse descriptions lead to victory: the final actions are consequences of the preceding sustained activity, with fa marking that result.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r6.claim: The pronoun refers to daybreak and the bā indicates time; dust is specified at dawn because its rising is not apparent at night.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r7.claim: Raising dust alludes to speed, intense charging, and repeated advance and retreat; Ibn Rawāḥa's verse supports the image.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r8.speaker: ابن رواحة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r8.claim: His line speaks of horses stirring dust from the sides of Kadāʾ.

ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r9.speaker: أبو عبيدة
ALUSI-FULL:v30p216/r9.claim: He says naqʿ can mean raising a cry, supported by Labīd's line about a truthful shout.

ELMALILI:100:4/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:4/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:4/r1.claim: The finite clause is coordinated with the preceding active participles, whose relative clauses carry verbal meaning; the shift to a finite verb signals the intended action occurring at this moment.

ELMALILI:100:4/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:4/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:4/r2.claim: Affecting, stirring, and driving the dust is the preferred sense of atharna from isāra, though seeking or tracking from athara is also possible.

ELMALILI:100:4/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:4/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:4/r3.claim: The pronoun in bih returns to morning; naqʿ chiefly means the dust raised during a raid, despite several other lexical senses.

ELMALILI:100:4/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:4/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:4/r4.claim: Dust may have risen during the earlier running too, but it was invisible at night and appeared by day; mentioning morning also implies the sparks came at night.

ELMALILI:100:4/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:4/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:4/r5.claim: The dust may also allude to the later discovery of gunpowder.

ELMALILI:100:4/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:100:4/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:100:4/r6.claim: Given naqʿ’s wider meanings, the verse may also hint at battle cries, sweat, and spilled blood during the assault.

QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r1.claim: The Meccan surah has eleven verses and moves in rapid, forceful jumps before settling at its ending, like a runner reaching the finish.

QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r2.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r2.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r2.claim: The opening scene shows charging, panting horses striking sparks, attacking at dawn, raising dust, and suddenly breaking into enemy ranks.

QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r6.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r6.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r6.claim: The rough, rumbling, cracking rhythm suits the noisy dust and forceful disclosure of graves and hearts, as well as the surah’s ingratitude and greed.

QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r7.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r7.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:100:1/r7.claim: The oath’s noisy cavalry scene frames the surah’s moral and resurrection scenes: image and frame mirror one another.

QUTB-ZILAL:100:4/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:100:4/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:100:4/r1.claim: The charge unexpectedly raises the dust of battle.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p500/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p500/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p500/r5.claim: The runners excite dust from the ground through the force of their gallop; naqʿ means dust.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p500/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p500/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p500/r6.claim: The preposition bi can mark cause, with its pronoun referring to running, or location, referring to the morning when they raided.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r2.claim: The fa introducing the stirred dust attaches the result to the raiding description: dust and reaching the crowd follow the dawn raid, rather than being independent oath objects.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r3.claim: The shift from active participles to two past-tense verbs moves from the oath to a narrative of the results of charging, sparking, and raiding: reaching the target.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r4.claim: If the chargers are warhorses, the target is an enemy settlement; if they are pilgrims' camels, dust rises on arrival and the “gathering” may be Muzdalifah.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r5.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r5.claim: Ali interpreted the chargers as pilgrimage mounts; that reading makes the oath by pilgrimage rites persuasive to disbelievers who deny the Qur'an's divine origin.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r6.claim: If the chargers are raiding horses, the oath alarms disbelievers with a looming raid, identified as Badr, while reassuring the Prophet about the troop he sent with al-Mundhir ibn Amr, if its report is sound.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p501/r7.claim: The specific horse oath also embeds reassurance for the Prophet about the dispatched unit's fate.

TABATABAI:100:1-5/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:100:1-5/r10.speaker: author
TABATABAI:100:1-5/r10.claim: Atharna means stirring up dust; a finite verb may follow active participles because they carry verbal force.

BINTSHATI:v1p108/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p108/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p108/r2.claim: The fāʾ connects raising dust to the dawn raid with immediate succession, matching the scene's speed.

BINTSHATI:v1p108/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p108/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v1p108/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī asks what fa-atharna coordinates with and says it follows the verb represented by the participle, meaning those that ran, sparked, and raised dust; Muḥammad ʿAbduh offers a similar analysis.

BINTSHATI:v1p108/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p108/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
BINTSHATI:v1p108/r4.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī refers the pronoun in bihi to dawn, meaning the horses raised dust at that time; this is also found in the Juzʾ ʿAmma commentary.

BINTSHATI:v1p108/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v1p108/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v1p108/r5.claim: Bint al-Shāṭiʾ prefers taking the pronoun as referring to the preceding raid, sparks, and running, understood from context.

CORPUSCORANICUM:100:4:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:4:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:4:anmerkung/r1.claim: The pronoun in bihī can plausibly refer to the place where the action occurs, as al-Ṭabarī explains.

CORPUSCORANICUM:100:4:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:4:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:100:4:anmerkung/r2.claim: Exegesis usually equates naqʿ with dust, but that explanation is isolated in Arabic lexicons; Lisān's sense of collected water may be preferable.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p416/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p416/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p416/r5.claim: Athara means raising or inciting and naqʿ means dust.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p417/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p417/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p417/r1.claim: If bihi refers to dawn, the assault raises a duststorm over the enemy; if it refers to the first verse's gallop, that gallop generates dust. Both portray a whirlwind attack.

STUDYQURAN:100:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:100:1/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:100:1/r4.claim: Pilgrimage camels rush from Mashʿar to Minā at dawn on the Day of Sacrifice.
